'''Christopher G. Tate''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|<small>FRS</small>]] (born 5 May 1964) is an English membrane protein biochemist and molecular biologist who works at the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in Cambridge, UK. Tate is known for his contributions to the understanding of [[G protein–coupled receptor|G protein-coupled receptors]].<ref name =mrc>{{Cite web|url=https://mrclmb.ac.uk/research-leaders/chris-tate/|title = Chris Tate}}</ref>

== Education ==

Tate was awarded the degree of BSc (Hons) in biochemistry by the [[University of Bristol]] in 1985. He was then awarded a PhD in 1989 by the [[University of Bristol]] for his work on integral membrane proteins in the red blood cell, under the supervision of Michael J. A. Tanner.<ref name=mrc />

== Career and research ==

Tate worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] (1989–1992) at the Department of Biochemistry, Cambridge, on bacterial sugar transporters in the group of Peter J. F. Henderson. After obtaining a research fellowship at [[Girton College, Cambridge]], he then moved in 1992 to the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology to work with [[Richard Henderson (biologist)|Richard Henderson]], initially on the [[serotonin transporter]] and then on the structure determination of the multidrug EmrE transporter<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ubarretxena-Belandia|first1=Iban|last2=Baldwin|first2=Joyce M.|last3=Schuldiner|first3=Shimon|last4=Tate|first4=Christopher G.|date=2003|title=Three-dimensional structure of the bacterial multidrug transporter EmrE shows it is an asymmetric homodimer|journal=The EMBO Journal|volume=22|issue=23|pages=6175–6181|doi=10.1093/emboj/cdg611|issn=0261-4189|pmc=291852|pmid=14633977}}</ref> by electron crystallography. Whilst working in Henderson's group, Tate developed the method of conformational thermostabilisation<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Serrano-Vega|first1=Maria J.|last2=Magnani|first2=Francesca|last3=Shibata|first3=Yoko|last4=Tate|first4=Christopher G.|date=2008|title=Conformational thermostabilization of the beta1-adrenergic receptor in a detergent-resistant form|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=105|issue=3|pages=877–882|doi=10.1073/pnas.0711253105|issn=1091-6490|pmc=2242685|pmid=18192400|bibcode=2008PNAS..105..877S|doi-access=free}}</ref> of [[G protein-coupled receptor]]s. This allowed the structure determination of the [[Beta-1 adrenergic receptor|beta1-adrenoceptor]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Warne|first1=Tony|last2=Serrano-Vega|first2=Maria J.|last3=Baker|first3=Jillian G.|last4=Moukhametzianov|first4=Rouslan|last5=Edwards|first5=Patricia C.|last6=Henderson|first6=Richard|last7=Leslie|first7=Andrew G. W.|last8=Tate|first8=Christopher G.|last9=Schertler|first9=Gebhard F. X.|date=2008|title=Structure of a beta1-adrenergic G-protein-coupled receptor|journal=Nature|volume=454|issue=7203|pages=486–491|doi=10.1038/nature07101|issn=1476-4687|pmc=2923055|pmid=18594507|bibcode=2008Natur.454..486W}}</ref> in collaboration with the group of Gebhard F.X. Schertler. The methodology was patented<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2008114020&recNum=141&docAn=GB2008000986&queryString=(ET/G%2520AND%2520ET/protein%2520AND%2520ET/coupled%2520AND%2520ET/receptors)%2520OR%2520(ABE/G%2520AND%2520ABE/protein%2520AND%2520ABE/coupled%2520AND%2520ABE/receptors)%2520OR%2520ET/GPCRs%2520OR%2520ABE/GPCRs%2520&maxRec=1148|title=World Intellectual Property Organization}}</ref> and used as the basis for the foundation of the drug discovery company Heptares Therapeutics Ltd<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heptares.com/|title=Heptares Ltd|access-date=2018-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826121522/https://www.heptares.com/|archive-date=2018-08-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> (HTL) in July 2007 by Tate, Henderson, Fiona Marshall (CSO) and Malcolm Weir (CEO).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scialom |first=Mike |date=2018-11-29 |title=It's a new day for Sosei Heptares |url=https://www.cambridgeindependent.co.uk/business/it-s-a-new-day-for-sosei-heptares-9050482/ |access-date=2023-09-27 |website=Cambridge Independent}}</ref>

Tate became an independent group leader in 2010 and since then his group has used structural biology to discover how the beta1-adrenoceptor<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Warne|first1=Tony|last2=Moukhametzianov|first2=Rouslan|last3=Baker|first3=Jillian G.|last4=Nehmé|first4=Rony|last5=Edwards|first5=Patricia C.|last6=Leslie|first6=Andrew G. W.|last7=Schertler|first7=Gebhard F. X.|last8=Tate|first8=Christopher G.|date=2011|title=The structural basis for agonist and partial agonist action on a β(1)-adrenergic receptor|journal=Nature|volume=469|issue=7329|pages=241–244|doi=10.1038/nature09746|issn=1476-4687|pmc=3023143|pmid=21228877|bibcode=2011Natur.469..241W}}</ref> and the [[adenosine A2A receptor]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lebon|first1=Guillaume|last2=Warne|first2=Tony|last3=Edwards|first3=Patricia C.|last4=Bennett|first4=Kirstie|last5=Langmead|first5=Christopher J.|last6=Leslie|first6=Andrew G. W.|last7=Tate|first7=Christopher G.|date=2011|title=Agonist-bound adenosine A2A receptor structures reveal common features of GPCR activation|journal=Nature|volume=474|issue=7352|pages=521–525|doi=10.1038/nature10136|issn=1476-4687|pmc=3146096|pmid=21593763}}</ref> are activated. In collaboration with the group of Reinhard Grisshammer (NIH, Bethesda), the structure of the thermostabilised [[neurotensin receptor]] was determined<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=White|first1=Jim F.|last2=Noinaj|first2=Nicholas|last3=Shibata|first3=Yoko|last4=Love|first4=James|last5=Kloss|first5=Brian|last6=Xu|first6=Feng|last7=Gvozdenovic-Jeremic|first7=Jelena|last8=Shah|first8=Priyanka|last9=Shiloach|first9=Joseph|date=2012|title=Structure of the agonist-bound neurotensin receptor|journal=Nature|volume=490|issue=7421|pages=508–513|doi=10.1038/nature11558|issn=1476-4687|pmc=3482300|pmid=23051748|bibcode=2012Natur.490..508W}}</ref> bound to a peptide agonist. Recent work has focused on understanding how G proteins coupled to G protein-coupled receptors,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=García-Nafría|first1=Javier|last2=Nehmé|first2=Rony|last3=Edwards|first3=Patricia C.|last4=Tate|first4=Christopher G.|date=2018|title=Cryo-EM structure of the serotonin 5-HT1B receptor coupled to heterotrimeric Go|journal=Nature|volume=558|issue=7711|pages=620–623|doi=10.1038/s41586-018-0241-9|issn=1476-4687|pmc=6027989|pmid=29925951|bibcode=2018Natur.558..620G}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Carpenter|first1=Byron|last2=Nehmé|first2=Rony|last3=Warne|first3=Tony|last4=Leslie|first4=Andrew G. W.|last5=Tate|first5=Christopher G.|date=2016|title=Structure of the adenosine A(2A) receptor bound to an engineered G protein|journal=Nature|volume=536|issue=7614|pages=104–107|doi=10.1038/nature18966|issn=1476-4687|pmc=4979997|pmid=27462812|bibcode=2016Natur.536..104C}}</ref> which has been facilitated by the development of mini-G proteins.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Carpenter|first1=Byron|last2=Tate|first2=Christopher G.|date=2016|title=Engineering a minimal G protein to facilitate crystallisation of G protein-coupled receptors in their active conformation|journal=Protein Engineering, Design & Selection |volume=29|issue=12|pages=583–594|doi=10.1093/protein/gzw049|issn=1741-0134|pmc=5181381|pmid=27672048}}</ref>

In 2021, Tate was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Christopher Tate {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/christopher-tate-35036/|access-date=2021-05-16|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref>
